title: How Mitsubishi Pencil Beat the Giant & Bought LAMY
description:
Stamped with three red diamonds, Mitsubishi Pencil states right on its website: "We have no affiliation with the Mitsubishi Group." How did this independent pen maker register the Mitsubishi trademark over a decade before the giant conglomerate—and acquire German fountain pen icon LAMY in 2024?
For anyone who grew up assuming Mitsubishi Pencil was a conglomerate side hustle, or ever wondered about the story behind uni and JETSTREAM.

Drawing on Mitsubishi Pencil Co., Ltd. (7976) official history and FAQ, FY2025 consolidated financial results, the 2024 announcement of the 100% acquisition of C. Josef Lamy GmbH, 2025–2026 press releases for LAMY safari JETSTREAM inside, LAMY safari KURUTOGA inside, and its color-only trademark, plus Mitsubishi Group's official history and trademark management records (mitsubishi.com), this video traces the full story: the 1887 waterwheel workshop in Naito-Shinjuku, the 1901 Ministry of Communications order and 1903 Trademark Registration No. 18865 filed 11 years ahead of the conglomerate, the 1958 wine-red uni and 2018 color trademark, the 100-million-a-year JETSTREAM and 17-year #1 KURUTOGA patent moats, and how buying 1930-founded LAMY pushed overseas revenue past 57% as the company targets ¥94 billion for its 140th anniversary in 2026.

This channel has no affiliation with any brands mentioned. Illustrations in this episode are AI-generated.
Data as of 2026-11-22

m001.text: Got a wine-red pencil or smooth pen on your desk?

m002.text: Three red diamonds—90% assume it's a giant's pen.

m003.text: A giant making cars, ships, and banks—why not pens?

m004.text: Mitsubishi Pencil says: no Mitsubishi Group ties!

m005.text: Wait—an even bigger twist is coming.

m006.text: It filed the Mitsubishi mark over 10 years earlier!

m007.text: In 2024, it even bought German pen icon LAMY!

m008.text: How did an independent pen maker pull all this off?

m009.text: We dug into Meiji trademark ledgers and financial data.

m010.text: Let's unpack this 100-year name clash and comeback!

m011.text: In 1870, Mitsubishi's Yataro Iwasaki began a shipping firm,

m012.text: flying three diamonds—starting a famed zaibatsu.

m013.text: It merged his lord's leaf crest with family diamonds.

m014.text: Three years on, Mitsubishi Shokai swept into finance!

m015.text: It was already famous—so how did a pencil shop file first?

m016.text: In 1878, Mitsubishi Pencil founder Niroku Masaki visited Paris.

m017.text: Seeing Western pencils at the Fair, he vowed to make them.

m018.text: Japan imported them all—no gear, no formulas, pure trial!

m019.text: In 1887, after 9 years, a Shinjuku waterwheel mill opened.

m020.text: He founded Masaki Manufacturing—but did it take off?

m021.text: It nearly failed: leads snapped and wood split easily!

m022.text: He refined lead and wood for 14 years to match import quality.

m023.text: In 1901, Japan's postal ministry adopted his pencils!

m024.text: It ordered three hardness grades for official use.

m025.text: Japan's first domestic state order—he wanted a proud mark.

m026.text: That quick sketch sparked a century-long coincidence!

m027.text: No zaibatsu in mind—he just used his family's scale crest.

m028.text: Three scales became three diamonds for the grades—Mitsubishi!

m029.text: In 1903, he filed Trademark Registration No. 18865.

m030.text: The giant didn't register it until 1914—11 years later!

m031.text: Mitsubishi Group guards its mark. Why no lawsuit?

m032.text: Today its committee controls over 4500 trademarks!

m033.text: In 140 countries, its site warns copycats of legal action.

m034.text: Yet for over a century, it couldn't touch this pen maker!

m035.text: First, the pen maker filed first, holding prior rights.

m036.text: Second, only stationery—zero clash with heavy industry.

m037.text: In 1952, Masaki unified its name as Mitsubishi Pencil.

m038.text: Sounds like a free ride on a famous name—was it really?

m039.text: Not at all! The name blocked Western luxury markets.

m040.text: Postwar pencils seemed cheap, and the West saw ships!

m041.text: Would you coast on a mix-up, or build a new brand?

m042.text: In 1958, it launched premium uni—truly one of a kind!

m043.text: To beat Western yellow and green, it tested 160 colors.

m044.text: It picked wine-red with black-and-gold rings: the uni hue!

m045.text: Rivals used paper boxes—it built a hinged plastic case!

m046.text: With smooth lead, hand-packing fell behind—instant prestige!

m047.text: In 1966 came Hi-uni, spanning 22 grades from soft 10B to hard 10H.

m048.text: Who buys extremes? Even piano tuners!

m049.text: It confirmed soft graphite lubricates piano key sides.

m050.text: And architects used the hardest grade to mark bricks!

m051.text: Out of the zaibatsu shadow with uni, by 2000,

m052.text: ballpoints and mechanical pencils ruled desks. How to break out?

m053.text: Two 100-million-seller patented pens built the war chest to buy LAMY!

m054.text: Remember old oil pens? Clumpy ink that easily smeared.

m055.text: Water ink dried slowly—2006 broke the deadlock!

m056.text: It launched low-viscosity oil ballpoint JETSTREAM, slashing drag!

m057.text: Smooth, fast-drying, rich black—over 100 million a year!

m058.text: Two years on, that obsession hit mechanical pencils.

m059.text: Hate how pencil lead wears flat, thickens, and snaps?

m060.text: For decades, people just rotated the pencil by hand.

m061.text: Engineers vowed: if hands won't turn it, the lead will!

m062.text: In 2008, KURUTOGA arrived with micro-gears inside the tip.

m063.text: Each time you lift the tip, pressure rotates the lead.

m064.text: A conical, sharp tip—clean lines and zero smudges!

m065.text: Over 100 million sold—number one in Japan for 17 years!

m066.text: Beyond engineering, it even locked down its iconic colors:

m067.text: 2018: uni's wine-red, black, and gold won a color trademark!

m068.text: With patents and color rights, what wall remained?

m069.text: Great at value tech, yet reliant on overseas dealers.

m070.text: Far from European taste, it missed upscale fountain pens.

m071.text: With a deep war chest, how would it flip the script?

m072.text: People expected a slow grind—then came 2024!

m073.text: It announced a full buyout of Heidelberg fountain pen legend LAMY!

m074.text: From zero shares before, it bought 100% in one bold sweep!

m075.text: Founded in 1930, LAMY is famed for Bauhaus design.

m077.text: Its 1980 safari pairs a triangular grip with a bold clip,

m078.text: gripping even thick denim—a global icon for over 40 years!

m079.text: Once thought a subsidiary, it bought a German design icon!

m080.text: You may wonder how a value Japanese firm fits German luxury.

m081.text: Put both firms side by side—it's a match made in heaven.

m082.text: No overlap: Japan brings refills, Germany design and retail.

m083.text: It also gained metal fountain-nib craft—the missing piece.

m084.text: Cross-border deals often stumble—could this duo ship hits?

m085.text: Fast work! By next January, the first fusion hit shelves.

m086.text: LAMY safari JETSTREAM inside packed ultra-smooth ink into a German barrel!

m087.text: Best of all for fans, its M17 refill even fits older LAMY pens.

m088.text: At ¥3630 a pen and ¥1100 a refill, it was an instant hit!

m089.text: March 2026 brought wave two: a self-turning pencil!

m090.text: LAMY safari KURUTOGA inside brought Japan's lead engine to the West.

m091.text: It built a seamless German barrel with a low-wobble engine.

m092.text: Priced at ¥4,180, it fused two design worlds into one!

m093.text: Forget hype—let's check FY2025 consolidated earnings!

m094.text: Guess how big this former waterwheel shop has grown today?

m095.text: Revenue hit ¥89.8 billion, with operating margins over 10%.

m096.text: Better yet: overseas sales hit ¥51.4 billion—over 57% total!

m097.text: Europe alone topped ¥17.1 billion—its top growth engine.

m098.text: German fixed assets hit ¥7.8 billion—second only to Japan!

m099.text: European destocking and costs cut operating profit by 20%,

m100.text: yet its equity ratio is 75%—filings say no parent company.

m101.text: It's expanding supply chains across Asia and the West,

m102.text: eyeing a record ¥94 billion for its 140th anniversary!

m103.text: Remember what 90% of people got wrong at the start?

m104.text: People think it rode a giant's name—it's the opposite!

m105.text: A 100-year fluke gave it a famous name, not world respect.

m106.text: Shedding that halo for deep engineering won the world stage!

m107.text: What turns a workshop into a giant isn't a shared name.

m108.text: It's generation after generation honing one tiny pen tip.

m109.text: Tell me in the comments: are you team JETSTREAM or team KURUTOGA?

m110.text: Love uncovering everyday truths? Don't forget to subscribe!
